title: Fly over Hunza: Baltit, Altit and Rakaposhi
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: This is the Hunza Valley, in Gilgit-Baltistan, at the heart of the Karakoram mountains.
Let's fly up the valley, following the Hunza River, between some of the highest peaks on Earth.
Ahead, on the green mountainside, is Karimabad, the old capital of the Hunza kingdom.
Above the town stands Baltit Fort. Its history goes back more than seven hundred years.
For centuries it was home to the Mirs, the rulers of Hunza, until the last Mir moved to a new palace in nineteen forty-five.
After years of decay, the Aga Khan Trust for Culture restored it, and in nineteen ninety-six it reopened as a museum.
Just along the valley is Altit Fort, built in the eleventh century, the oldest surviving monument in the region.
It stands on rock more than a thousand feet above the Hunza River, and its restoration won a UNESCO heritage award in twenty eleven.
These forts guarded a valley linked to the ancient Silk Road, and many people here still speak Burushaski, a language unrelated to any other known language.
Now, let's turn around, and look to the south-west.
That is Rakaposhi, rising seven thousand, seven hundred and eighty-eight metres above sea level.
Its snowy face towers over the valley, and the view from Karimabad is one of the most famous in Pakistan.
